comments.body:
## Where the 0.13.0 MCP release stands

Release ticket: hyperbolic-pernicious-drongo (c066-c496-7012-4a39), in_progress. It had NO dependencies at the start of this session -- nothing connected it to any MCP work, so "ship MCP stable" had no defined done. Five package-level blockers are now linked `blocks` it:

  dbca-97ac-ad96-4d6d  CLOSED certified   MCP LLM-tier error classification
  e1d9-4c8e-3fd1-41c2  in_progress        /health cannot see the request path -- code MERGED (2362)
  494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0  in_progress        list_tickets can close the transport -- code MERGED (2355)
  505d-b2c5-734f-47d9  in_progress        claim gate FAILS OPEN on unresolvable ref -- code MERGED (2357)
  aefe-614a-2631-4117  in_progress        reads return [] for a broken store -- BLOCKED, see below

FOUR of five have merged code. They remain in_progress because their acceptance criteria are not yet evidenced and ticked. That gap -- code lands, ticket never closes -- was the most common failure this session: a sweep found SIX in_progress tickets whose fix was already on main and which nobody had closed, three merged days earlier.

## Framing that should survive

0.13.0 ships a PyPI package. "MCP stable" splits into (a) the package users install and (b) our on-box deployment. Most incident work here -- review-bot 502, nginx edge, terraform, Jira credentials, disk reclaim -- is (b) and does NOT block the tag. Treating every live alarm as release-critical wasted effort early.

## Operator decision recorded

Certification environment is NOT a gate. Any certification is as good as any other now; restricting to a trusted set is a FUTURE feature. Implemented in 2361 (MERGED): verify_opcert_record no longer refuses on principal mismatch; trust root picked strongest-first (own_key -> pinned_environment -> envelope_key), surfaced as a typed trust_basis field. Under verify.require_environment the envelope_key fallback is WITHHELD, so enforcement binds to the pinned key, never to a key the cert supplies about itself. Settles item (a) of ADR ticket 987c-67d0-258e-4069.

## Highest-value open findings

1. aefe (P1) -- THE APPROVED PLAN IS WRONG; redesign before anything lands. materialize_tickets builds the pinned ticket store as a BARE TREE with no .git, so a .git-less tracker dir is BOTH the poisoned production volume AND a legitimate gate snapshot. The approved .git-presence predicate rejects both, making every pinned ticket read by plan-review and completion-verifier raise store_uninitialized -- a P1 regression from a P1 fix. Full-suite proof: 6 failed / 17843 passed. A parallel session has the same defective predicate at ~/fix-rapt-read-semantics.
2. 9d40-1db8-1bcc-4f91 (P1) -- review-bot zombie. A compose recreate SIGTERMs the bot; uvicorn closes its LISTENING SOCKET at the start of graceful shutdown, then lifespan shutdown never returns because in-flight reviews keep running. Container reports Up, worker keeps voting ~18 min, nothing bound to port 8000. Dispatch died 22 minutes and, since the Gerrit webhooks plugin is not at-least-once (ADR 0009), events in that window were DROPPED. Silent by construction. The shipped MCP server is NOT vulnerable: drain_then_exit is bounded by grace_seconds (verified).
3. 1d1b-a719-b675-4a1f (P2) -- infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template is in NONE of autodeploy's six path manifests, so edge config is outside change detection and fails SILENTLY. a61d's merged fix cannot go live by itself.
4. eb67-b96c-dcf0-4f86 (P1) -- terraform state holds 23 real secrets in cleartext. CONTAINED: S3 rebar-tfstate-896586841071, SSE-S3, no bucket policy, EC2 role gets implicitDeny, only the admin IAM user allowed -- a box compromise does not yield state. NOT contained: 149 retained object versions, so rotating a secret does not remove it from history.
5. 5caa-4b63-7ea2-4e71 -- pinning uv (2367, MERGED) removed only ONE of two manifest consumers. setup-uv also calls getArtifact(...manifestUrl) UNCONDITIONALLY for the download URL and a hosted runner always reaches it, so the fetch-failed mode is NOT eliminated. The original ticket's acceptance criterion was unachievable as written.

## CI reliability -- there were no flakes

Every Verified -1 investigated was deterministic:
  2359 -- gitutil.py 833 vs the 800 cap, identical on all four platforms
  2360 / 2362 -- broad `except Exception` on the MCP boot path without the required RemovedInputError guard
  2361 -- types.py stale; a hand-edited GENERATED file had WIDENED trust_basis from the schema Literal to str
  2345 -- a real test failure
Two failures were mislabelled "environmental" by misreading the workflow ECHOING ITS OWN SCRIPT SOURCE as error output. Tell: genuine failures are ##[error] lines WITHOUT the 36;1m colour prefix.

## The recurring defect class -- including in this session's own work

Checks that cannot distinguish the states they are meant to separate:
  - watcher condition `grep -qE "^(FAILED|ERROR)"` can NEVER fire (ANSI codes precede the word); five loops leaked
  - `gh run view --job=N --log` returns an EMPTY log while the parent run is in progress -> 0/0/0 on all greps
  - duplicate-detection grep whose PREFIX matched two genuinely distinct historical entries
  - idempotency check using `git diff` against HEAD, which reports drift regardless
  - scope detector matching `^def ` but not `async def`, naming the wrong enclosing function
Anchor every check on a known-present positive BEFORE asserting the property.

## Process hazards for the next session

- ANOTHER SESSION pushes under the same RebarBotNava identity. Duplicate changes on e127 (2347 vs 2351) and 6bf1 (2344 vs 2352); two sessions wrote into ONE worktree (~/rebar-wt-e127), one amending the other's uncommitted work. Check a change's rebar-ticket trailer before assuming it is yours.
- REBASE BY current_revision, never a hardcoded patchset ref. Rebasing 2355 from refs/changes/55/2355/1 silently discarded fixture fixes already pushed in response to a CI failure.
- CHANGELOG.md is a live conflict hotspot: every merge invalidates every other in-flight change touching it, and rebasing DROPS both votes.
- _mcp_health.py ~777/800 and is where boot-path work lands; gitutil.py landed at 798/800 (split filed as f802-536b-0081-432a).
- For bugfix-size-attestation the remedy is a TICKET action plus rerun-llm-review -- NOT amend+push, which trips changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE and carries the -1 forward unreviewed.

## Unreconciled, flagged not hidden

On 879b, `verify-signature --kind plan-review` reports certified while `review-plan --status` reports stale-code naming three file_impact deps -- even when passed --ref at the exact SHA the attestation was signed against. The two views disagree; not reconciled. Recorded on Gerrit 2360.

## Shutdown addendum

### Landed after the main entry
- Gerrit 2369 'Split the git lock policy out of gitutil' pushed for review (NOT submitted), ticket f802-536b-0081-432a in_progress. gitutil.py 798 -> 373, new git_locking.py 484. Plan-review took 5 runs, 4 genuine BLOCK rounds, no --force. Its first attestation went stale mid-review because docs/concurrency.md landed on origin/main; re-ran and claimed back-to-back to close the window.
  NEXT SESSION: wait for both votes on 2369, Submit, THEN close f802 -- not before it merges.
- The monkeypatch-retarget evidence on that change is the model to copy: 6 of 7 moved names are structurally protected (not re-exported, so raising=True makes a mis-target loud), ONE (_backoff_sleep) is legitimately re-exported and therefore silently mis-targetable -- proven with a seeded mutant where the correct target catches it and the old target passes vacuously. It also declined to claim proof for gitutil.os / gitutil.subprocess, because those are the same stdlib module objects as git_locking's and so are not module-sensitive seams. Honest non-claims are worth as much as the proofs.
- A second vacuity channel found there: getattr(gitutil, '_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S', 300) falls through silently AND the real constant is 300, so a value comparison proves nothing. Needed a sentinel default.

### Open Gerrit changes at shutdown (mine, none submittable)

### Merged in the closing stretch
2353, 2354, 2355, 2356, 2357, 2358, 2359, 2361, 2362, 2363, 2364, 2366, 2367. 42 commits reached main in 18 hours.

dewy-rotatable-tarsier (d240), taurine-smiling-hamadryad (9bc0), cibophobic-moist-guineafowl (b928), seaborne-wisdomless-songbird (dd96, obsolete), dire-expectable-terrapin (d26a), oozy-darkish-merganser (daa7), colourless-hasteless-lamb (5ec7), potential-powellite-mouflon (dbca).

- /Users/joeoakhart/rebar is on main, clean apart from the two pre-existing reb-3115-*.py untracked files.
- 67 worktrees remain. Deliberately NOT pruned: another session is active under the same identity and removing worktrees mid-flight already disrupted one change earlier tonight. Prune only after confirming no session is live.

## Final addendum -- last subagent wound down

### Closes
- dying-dietary-bass (bc5d-ffba-006b-4241) CLOSED, verify-signature --kind completion-verifier -> certified. NINTH certified close this session. Closed --ref fafe25e0d1abfbade07d22c51f599672e7ac1707 (the LATER of its two referencing commits; 77fc1b99 is its ancestor, so the verified tree carries both). The file_impact union trap resolved to a no-op -- fafe25e0 touched only the workflow file 77fc1b99 had introduced -- so NO set-file-impact call was made and the attestation's material stayed intact.
- seagreen-fortuitous-crayfish (f449-be6a-be56-4fef) NOT closed, correctly. The attestation-laundering gate refused it: the AC3 provenance justification NAMED the two live test symbols, which makes a [non-codebase] criterion look repo-verifiable. Remedy (on the ticket) is to split AC3 -- repo-verifiable half untagged, external outcome tagged -- which is a material edit needing a fresh 15-20 min review-plan. NOT forced. Close class already decided: preexisting.
  WARNING for whoever resumes it: 3b92fad7 is a BAD --ref pin. run_differs.py and test_dc_rich_text_live.py both changed on main AFTER the fix, so a review pinned there goes stale-code immediately. Its earned plan-review PASS is at --ref ae4f6c1a.

### New ticket filed
feldspar-extinct-sambar (79a4-eae7-e5c7-4713), P2, discovered_from f449: deleting the refresh_scoped_snapshot(ctx) call at run_differs.py:237 SURVIVES the entire 3637-test reconciler suite. The overlay's BEHAVIOUR is well covered (5 tests kill a behaviour mutant, with an anchored clobber pair and a negative control) but its WIRING is not -- only the live DC lane catches the deletion. That asymmetry is the trap: a well-tested module reads as protected while its single invocation is unguarded. Acute right now because several src/rebar modules are being split for module-size reasons, and extraction is exactly the operation that drops call sites.

### Two smaller findings
- WRONG ADR CITATION in shipped source: 'ADR 0037 s3' appears in f449's body and TWICE in snapshot_lagfree_refresh.py's docstring. ADR 0037 is oss-contribution-intake-posture; the real support is docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md:282. Folded into 79a4's description to fix in the same change.
- ENVIRONMENT TRAP: FORCE_COLOR=3 exported in the operator shell makes 21 tests/interfaces CLI-help tests fail spuriously on ANSI codes; unset, all 121 pass. Same class as the anthropic-1.2.0 venv artifact -- an environment condition that reads as repository evidence. Unset it before any suite run.

### Machine state, final
Zero processes remain from any subagent (the last one killed three of its own waiter loops that were spinning on a condition that could never fire -- the same never-fires pattern seen five times tonight). No unpushed commits outstanding. /Users/joeoakhart/rebar on main, clean apart from the two pre-existing reb-3115-*.py untracked files.
